title: Jefferson-era legation codes Nos. 10, 13 and 16: residual groups in Short 1792, Carmichael 1788 and Thomas Pinckney 1793 (catalogue 484)

steps.what: Catalogue 484 brief (Founders Online sweep): Short 26 Jul 1792 Code No. 10 (401, 1083, 401; 359, 199, 34, 724 undeciphered), Carmichael 14 Apr 1788 Code No. 13 (conjectural), T. Pinckney 28 Aug 1793 Code No. 16 (deciphered in part, 497 undeciphered).
Founders texts through the built-in browser (plain HTTP blocked); LoC item JSON gave mtj1 016_0998-1009 (Short) and 009_0223-0230 (Carmichael); master JPEGs from tile.loc.gov.
Short's private letter of 27 Jul 1792 (016_1010-1012) re-enciphers the paragraph with the same groups and no decoding: digits confirmed, no plaintext.
Code No. 10 values on 016_1007-1008 sorted by number to test alphabetical bracketing: no ordered run (two-part code); bracketing ruled out.
Carmichael's groups looked up in the Code No. 11 table rebuilt in jefferson1787: 597 = freedom, 223 = trouble there; Code No. 13 is a different code. Founders 'Code No. 13' = this letter only.
Pinckney despatches found on NARA M30 roll 2 (catalog media server): 28 Aug 1793 = frame 0140; frames 0101-0330 downloaded (dl_m30.py).

Subagent transcribed all code on 15 coded Pinckney frames (~2,660 rows) with George Taylor's interlinear decodings (20 Jun, 25 Sep, 27 Nov, 17 Dec 1793, 28 Jan, Feb 1794) and the 25 Nov 1793 Explication aligned by hand.

28 Aug 1793 groups checked against the attested Code No. 16 values: 30 of 58 confirmed (to be, with, general-s, and, under him, des-tina-tion, general-ly thought, for); 447, 234, 501 occur nowhere else.
First group re-read at 2x: two matching open 4s, 447 (the editors printed 497).

Search of the 39 Code No. 10 documents (Founders notes, six letters on the images, ~1,100 groups of 31 May 1793): 401, 1083, 359, 199, 34, 724 occur only in the 26 Jul 1792 passage; 'been' = 1700, not 401.
Subagent transcribed all 674 code groups of Short's 26 Jul 1792 letter with TJ's interlinear (511 groups under a TJ word).
Web search for the number of regiments in Grey's force (Aug 1793) as a crib for 447: nothing specific.
reading.tsv measured: 737 groups, 728 with a reading (720 without conjectures), 9 open single-occurrence groups.

outcome.method_basis: The readings are Jefferson's interlinear decoding of Short's letter and the Jefferson Papers editors' printed decodings of all three; the work transcribed every group, checked them against values attested in sibling letters of the same code, and searched the siblings for the open groups.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.tsv: 737 counted code groups (one struck group excluded), 720 with a reading, 8 more by conjecture only (counted unread), 9 open

outcome.notes: Everything readable was read before (TJ's interlinear; PTJ editors). Added: 447 for the printed 497; 30 of the 58 Pinckney groups confirmed from Taylor's decodings; Code No. 13 shown not to be Code No. 11; 'been' = 1700 in Code No. 10, so the editors could not have meant 401 = been without a homophone; full transcriptions of Short's 674 groups and of Pinckney's 15 coded frames.

texts.label: William Short to Jefferson, The Hague, 26 Jul 1792 (Code No. 10)
texts.summary: Short's private complaint at being passed over for Paris in favour of Gouverneur Morris: Lafayette's mortification, the French diplomatic committee's wish to refuse Morris, and Short's preferences for a post (the Hague as resident, Spain as plenipotentiary) and for the grades of the American diplomatic establishment.

reading_review.note: The coded paragraphs read through as Short's sentences (Jefferson's interlinear on 511 groups, the editors' reading on the rest); two short holes: 401/1083/401 and 359 199 34 724.

texts.label: William Carmichael to Jefferson, Madrid, 14 Apr 1788 (Code No. 13)
texts.summary: A clear letter with five code numbers used as a test of his cypher: Maryland (twice), Massachusetts and the majority on the ratification of the Constitution; the last item (597) stays open. The read share of 0% counts only the five code groups: none has a value attested in another letter (four are context conjectures, 597 is open), and the clear text of the letter is not counted.

reading_review.note: Two sentences of clear text with four code names read by context (Maryland, Massachusetts, majority) and one open item (597).

texts.label: Thomas Pinckney to Jefferson, London, 28 Aug 1793 (Code No. 16)
texts.summary: Three coded sentences: regiments are to embark shortly on a secret expedition under Sir Charles Grey with Generals Stuart and Dundas, generally thought to be for the West Indies; the number of regiments (447) stays open.

reading_review.note: Three coherent sentences; the number of regiments (447) open and two words ([time], [secret]) conjectural.

prior.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson vols. 13 (1956), 24 (1990) and 26 (1995), via Founders Online: the three letters printed decoded from partial reconstructions of Codes 10, 13 and 16, conjectures in brackets, named groups undeciphered.
